terms.latin: sōle adustus, sōle adusta, sōle adustum
terms.gloss: sunburnt, scorched or browned by the sun
evidence: Plin. NH 19.19: in dēsertīs adustīsque sōle (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 27.47: sī quī forte adustiōris colōris, ut ex recentī viā, essent
terms.comment: Latin says it of the person: sōle adustus, scorched by the sun. The participle of adūrō, “scorch”; the verb serves too: sōle adūrī, get sunburnt. For the brown of a tan, see “suntan”.

terms.gloss: a burn; here, a burn from the sun
evidence: Plin. NH 32.34: ulcera frīgore aut adustiōne facta (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Pliny’s word for a burn on the skin, whatever its cause. We have found no ancient noun for a burn from the sun alone.

phrases.latin: Nisi in umbrā manēbis, sōle adūrēris.
phrases.english: If you don’t stay in the shade, you’ll get sunburnt.

phrases.latin: Umerī tuī sōle adustī sunt; unguentō eōs lēniter ungam.
phrases.english: Your shoulders are sunburnt; I’ll rub some cream on them gently.

phrases.latin: sī quī forte adustiōris colōris, ut ex recentī viā, essent
phrases.english: whether any were more sunburnt than the rest, as men fresh from a march would be

sources: Lewis & Short: adustio · Lewis & Short: aduro
